extracted.intended_audience: securities exchanges, SEC staff, securities lawyers, and regulated market participants who file or monitor Exchange Act rule filings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and drafting standards for submitting, publishing, and tracking a proposed rule change by a national securities exchange under Section 19(b) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 19b-4, including Commission action timelines, related-document metadata, and public-inspection practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory filing basis (Section 19(b)(1) and Rule 19b-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule change by an exchange must be filed with the Commission pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice cites BZX's April 15, 2024 filing 'pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) ... and Rule 19b-4.' Filers should identify the statutory and rule authority in the submission and use Rule 19b-4 formatting and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication for public comment in the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule changes are published in the Federal Register to solicit public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule change was published for comment (example: published May 1, 2024). Filers should expect their submission to be placed on public notice and allow time for comment periods before final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission designation of a longer period for action (Section 19(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may designate a longer period under Section 19(b)(2) within which it will approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings regarding a proposed rule change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: On May 30, 2024, the Commission designated a longer period for action. Filers should anticipate that the statutory review period can be extended and monitor Commission notices for such designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution of proceedings to determine disapproval (Section 19(b)(2)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may institute proceedings pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) to determine whether to disapprove a proposed rule change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: On July 12, 2024, the Commission instituted proceedings under 19(b)(2)(B). Such proceedings signal further substantive review and may include additional record development or briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange withdrawal of a proposed rule change
rubrics_metrics.description: An exchange may withdraw a previously filed proposed rule change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Exchange withdrew SR‑CboeBZX‑2024‑026 on November 8, 2024. Filers should follow Commission procedures and file a notice of withdrawal if they choose to terminate the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document metadata and heading elements required in Federal Register notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register documents typically include specific heading/metadata elements that identify the issuing agency, CFR titles/parts affected, docket numbers, and RINs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists common headings: the agency or agencies issuing the document; the CFR title and part numbers amended or related; agency docket/internal file number; and the RIN. See the Document Drafting Handbook for detailed drafting conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official PDF/govinfo.gov for legal/evidentiary purposes; verify XML against official edition
rubrics_metrics.description: The FederalRegister.gov XML rendition is an unofficial prototype; the official electronic format and legal edition is the PDF on govinfo.gov or the official printed Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cautions that the XML prototype does not replace the official edition and that users relying on content for legal research should verify against the official edition. Only official editions provide legal notice and judicial notice under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection and FR Doc identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register documents have a public-inspection record identifying the FR Doc number, and the public inspection PDF shows the date/time it appeared on public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'This PDF is FR Doc. 2024-26753 as it appeared on Public Inspection on 11/15/2024 at 8:45 am.' Those using public inspection listings for research should verify contents against the final edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related-documents and docket-tracking practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices identify and link related documents in the same agency docket (e.g., prior releases, orders, and notices related to the same file number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page displays five related documents (with dates and titles) connected to File No. SR‑CboeBZX‑2024‑026. Filers and reviewers should track related Federal Register entries and release numbers to follow the procedural history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature block and delegation statement in Commission notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission notices include an attribution/signature block indicating the office or official issuing the notice and any delegated authority statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example text: 'For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority. Sherry R. Haywood, Assistant Secretary.' Filings and notices should include appropriate signature, office identification, and delegation citations (e.g., 17 CFR 200.30-3(a)(12)).
